headline: Connecticut flood survivors can seek SBA loans after September disaster declaration
dek: The federal designation covers Fairfield, New Haven and Litchfield counties; a Bridgeport center opens Oct. 7, with physical-damage applications due Dec. 1.
body: People whose homes, belongings or businesses were damaged by Connecticut’s Sept. 13 flash flooding can begin applying for low-interest federal disaster loans after the U.S. Small Business Administration approved a disaster declaration for Fairfield County and the contiguous Connecticut counties of New Haven and Litchfield. Gov. Ned Lamont announced the designation Tuesday. The [Connecticut governor’s office](https://portal.ct.gov/governor/news/press-releases/2026/10-2026/governor-lamont-secures-sba-disaster-declaration-for-september-13-flooding) said joint assessments by federal, state and local officials found damage above the threshold for SBA assistance.

The declaration reaches several groups at once. The governor’s office says homeowners may seek up to $500,000 to repair a primary residence, while homeowners and renters may qualify for up to $100,000 to replace damaged or destroyed personal property. Businesses can apply for up to $2 million for physical losses involving real estate, inventory, machinery and equipment. Businesses and private nonprofits may also seek Economic Injury Disaster Loans of up to $2 million for working capital while normal operations are disrupted.

The limits are maximum loan amounts, not automatic awards. Applicants still have to submit information to the SBA and qualify under the agency’s disaster-loan rules. The [Federal Register notice](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/06/2026-20472/administrative-declaration-of-a-disaster-for-the-state-of-connecticut) describes the action as an administrative declaration issued Oct. 2 for severe storms and flash flooding. It lists Fairfield as the primary county and New Haven and Litchfield as contiguous Connecticut counties, and sets interest rates that vary by applicant type and whether the applicant has credit available elsewhere.

That distinction matters for residents trying to understand what has been approved. This announcement opens an SBA loan program; it is not an announcement that FEMA grants or other forms of major-disaster aid have been awarded. The federal notice says physical-damage loan applications are due Dec. 1, 2026. Applications for economic-injury loans are due July 2, 2027. The state says residents can apply through the [MySBA Loan Portal](https://lending.sba.gov/), where applicants can submit forms and later review loan details and payments.

A temporary in-person Disaster Loan Outreach Center is scheduled to open Wednesday, Oct. 7, at the Margaret E. Morton Government Center, 999 Broad St., in Bridgeport. According to the governor’s office, the center will generally operate from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. Monday through Friday and from 9 a.m. to 1 p.m. Saturday, with no Sunday hours. It will close at 2 p.m. Oct. 9, operate on adjusted hours Oct. 20 and 21, close for the Columbus Day holiday on Oct. 12, and is expected to shut permanently at 4 p.m. Oct. 21.

The assistance arrives as recovery work continues weeks after the storm. The [American Red Cross](https://www.redcross.org/local/connecticut/about-us/news-and-events/press-releases/red-cross-continues-fairfield-county-flood-response-and-recovery0.html) said Sept. 23 that it estimated more than 1,000 homes had been affected in Fairfield County and that more than 75 volunteers had been helping assess damage, provide recovery support, deliver meals and connect residents with resources. That estimate is from the Red Cross’s response work, not a final state or federal damage tally.

[News 12 reported Tuesday](https://longisland.news12.com/2026/10/06/flood-victims-in-fairfield-county-gain-access-to-sba-recovery-loans/ctm3wPT4TEZ3HW2ghCzSB) that homeowners, renters, businesses and nonprofits in Fairfield County and parts of western Connecticut can now seek the loans, and that the Bridgeport center will help applicants. The new designation also gives residents a concrete next step after state officials spent the first weeks documenting losses and weighing what type of federal assistance might be available. Applicants should preserve repair records, photographs, insurance information and other damage documentation, then confirm current eligibility and deadlines directly with the SBA.

For communities along the southwestern Connecticut coast and in neighboring inland counties, the practical question is whether a low-interest loan can cover costs that insurance or savings will not. The public record confirms the counties, program limits, deadlines and outreach location, but it does not yet provide a final statewide dollar estimate for the flood. The next visible step is the Bridgeport center’s opening, followed by the Dec. 1 deadline for physical-damage applications and continued local recovery efforts.
location: Fairfield, New Haven and Litchfield counties, Connecticut
author: NorthEast News Desk
seoTitle: Connecticut flood survivors can seek SBA disaster loans
seoDescription: An SBA disaster declaration opens low-interest loans for flood-damaged homes, belongings, businesses and nonprofits in three Connecticut counties.
